paper_id: Dong et al. - 2009 - Dynamic Linking and Loading in Networked Embedded Systems
title: Dynamic Linking and Loading in Networked Embedded Systems
motivation: WSN nodes deployed in inaccessible environments need over-the-air reprogramming, but existing approaches either cost too much energy to disseminate (bootloader) or to execute (VM).
problem_framing: Design a dynamic linking/loading mechanism for micro sensor nodes meeting four requirements: minimal code size, efficient execution/loading, portable design, and isolated kernel/application development.
key_insight: Use pre-relocating and pre-linking at compile-time to shift work offline, and maintain a kernel jump table to decouple application layout from kernel layout, enabling isolated updates.
method_signature: Transform standard ELF to minimized SELF format; employ pre-relocating+pre-linking at compile-time; use kernel jump table for kernel/application isolation.
evaluation_criteria: Code size ratio (SELF vs ELF/CELF), loading speed improvement percentage (pre-relocating+pre-linking vs standard mechanism), portability across MicaZ/TelosB.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Tradeoff acknowledged: data encoding can further reduce code size but incurs decoding overhead during loading, and delta patching limits flexibility for heterogeneous networks.
evidence_for_taste: clean isolation between kernel and application
our approach can be easily ported
thinking_moves: 识别现有方案在能耗两端的矛盾：dissemination vs execution
把运行时开销前移到编译时，用pre-relocating/pre-linking换取加载速度
